q: The simple form of: Though he has a busy schedule, he finds time to exercise.
o: In spite of his having a busy schedule, he finds time to exercise.
In spite of his being a busy schedule, he finds time to exercise.
Despite of his having a busy schedule, he finds time to exercise.
Because of his having a busy schedule, he finds time to exercise.

q: She is too young to drive a car. (Compound sentence)
o: She is very young and canot drive a car.
She is very young and cannot drive a car.
She is very young and so that cannot drive a car.
She is very young and that cannot drive a car.
e: too ... to যুক্ত simple sentence-কে compound করতে too-এর জায়গায় very বসে, to-এর জায়গায় and বসে, তারপর tense অনুযায়ী cannot বা could not আসে, শেষে to-এর পরের অংশ যায়। তাই She is very young and cannot drive a car। আরেকটি উদাহরণ: He is very busy and cannot attend the meeting। অন্য বিকল্পে that ও so that বেমানান।

q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Do you know what he is doing what?
Do you know what he is doing?
You know what is he doing?
Do you know what is he doing?
e: Do you know what he is doing? বাক্যে একটি প্রশ্ন অন্য একটি প্রশ্নের ভেতরে বসেছে (embedded বা indirect question)। এ ধরনের প্রশ্নে question word থাকলেও শব্দক্রম সাধারণ বাক্যের মতো subject + verb হয়, inversion হয় না। তাই what he is doing শুদ্ধ। What is he doing হলো সরাসরি প্রশ্নের গঠন, যা এখানে ভুল। What শেষে আবার বসানোও অপ্রয়োজনীয়।
